 The Nations League reaches its decisive final round with Germany, Italy, France and Denmark battling for quarter-final places. Here is what every League A team needs.

 The UEFA Nations League enters its decisive final round between 15 and 17 November, with several European heavyweights still fighting for places in the 2027 quarter-finals . Italy, France, Germany, the Netherlands and Denmark all face important tests, while Spain, England and Portugal have already secured qualification.
 The top two teams from each League A group advance to the quarter-finals, but the battle for group supremacy, survival and relegation remains open. Here is what every team needs heading into the final fixtures.
 Group A1: Italy, France and Belgium in a three-way battle
 Italy (10 points) will qualify if they avoid defeat against Belgium. A victory guarantees first place, while a draw will also be enough to win the group if France fail to beat Türkiye.
 France (10 points) need a draw against Türkiye to guarantee qualification. Didier Deschamps' side will win the group if they beat Türkiye and Italy fail to defeat Belgium.
 Belgium (9 points) must beat Italy to reach the quarter-finals. They could even finish first if they win and France fail to beat Türkiye.
 Türkiye (0 points) are already confirmed in fourth place, although their final result could influence whether they suffer automatic relegation or enter the play-offs.
 Group A2: Germany face a decisive Netherlands showdown
 Netherlands (11 points) will secure first place with a draw against Germany. They will also qualify for the quarter-finals if Greece fail to beat Serbia.
 Germany (8 points) could finish first with victory over the Dutch, provided Greece fail to beat Serbia. A draw would also secure a quarter-final place if Greece lose.
 Greece (8 points) will qualify if they defeat Serbia and Germany fail to beat the Netherlands. They could also progress without winning if Germany lose.
 Serbia (0 points) are already confirmed in fourth place and cannot reach the quarter-finals. Their final result could still influence the relegation arrangements.
 Group A3: England must beat Spain to finish first
 Spain (15 points) and England (12 points) have both qualified for the quarter-finals. Their meeting in Madrid will determine the group winners.
 Spain need only a draw, while England must win to overtake the European champions. Thomas Tuchel's side secured qualification with their 2-1 victory over Croatia on Thursday.
 Croatia (3 points) need only avoid defeat against Czechia to secure third place. Czechia (0 points) must win to escape the bottom position.
 Group A4: Portugal under pressure after Denmark humiliation
 Portugal (12 points) remain top despite their shocking 4-1 home defeat against Denmark . They have already qualified and will finish first if they avoid defeat against Wales or Denmark fail to beat Norway.
 Denmark (9 points) will secure qualification by avoiding defeat against Norway. They could win the group if they beat Norway and Portugal lose to Wales.
 Norway (6 points) must defeat Denmark to reach the quarter-finals. Any other result will leave them facing the League A/B play-offs.
 Wales (3 points) are confirmed in fourth place but could still avoid automatic relegation. A draw or victory against Portugal would guarantee them a place in the League A/B play-offs.
 All eight remaining League A fixtures kick off at 20:45 CET . The quarter-final and promotion/relegation play-off draw is scheduled for Friday, 20 November, with the quarter-finals taking place in March 2027.
